 BCVN 
 Banque Cantonale Vaudoise has delivered a strong share price run in recent years, and that naturally raises a question for anyone looking at the stock today. Is the current price of the bank justified by the returns it earns on the capital entrusted to it? 
 Over the past 5 years the share price return of 121.6% puts real weight on the issue of whether Banque Cantonale Vaudoise's capital returns are strong enough to support that kind of market optimism about the business. 
 The bank's model as a cantonal lender with a focus on interest income, fee activities and balance sheet strength can concentrate the valuation discussion on how efficiently it reinvests earnings and compounds capital for shareholders over time. 
 If you'd rather focus on earnings, this one's for you. See what Banque Cantonale Vaudoise's 25.9x P/E says about the price . 
 The stock's next move may depend on whether the returns Banque Cantonale Vaudoise earns on its capital are high and consistent enough to make today's share price look reasonable. 
 If you are evaluating how effectively Banque Cantonale Vaudoise converts capital into shareholder returns, it can be useful to compare this pattern with a broader set of 218 resilient stocks with low risk scores . 
 Has Banque Cantonale Vaudoise Run Too Far on Excess Returns? 
 The Excess Returns model looks at how much profit Banque Cantonale Vaudoise can earn above its cost of equity and how long that can last. For this bank, the framework leans heavily on a stable earnings profile, with book value of CHF46.28 per share and stable EPS of CHF5.26 per share based on the median return on equity from the past 5 years. The model uses a cost of equity of CHF2.18 per share and estimates excess return of CHF3.08 per share, paired with an average return on equity of 11.51% and a stable book value of CHF45.71 per share. 
 Taken together, the Excess Returns and dividend assumptions present a picture of a mature lender where value is supported by steady profitability and sizeable distributions. The dividend model uses a CHF4.60 per share payout, an 83.98% payout ratio and modest long term growth near 0.59%, resulting in a present value estimate that sits close to but below the current CHF132.70 share price. The Excess Returns projections put Banque Cantonale Vaudoise's estimated intrinsic value modestly below the current share price.
